fields.author: Ada Marlow
fields.standfirst: Boards, thread and glue, and what each of them says about how long a book was meant to last.
fields.image_alt: Two open books side by side on a bench
fields.body:
Pick up two copies of the same title, thirty years apart, and the difference is in the spine before it is anywhere else.

Sewn, glued, or neither

A sewn book opens flat and stays open. A glued one is cheaper to make and, in time, cheaper to throw away. Neither is a moral failing; they are answers to different questions.

A book is a machine for staying open at the right page.

We keep a small shelf of rebound copies at the back. They are not first editions and they are not worth anything, and they will outlast almost everything else in the shop.

fields.author: Rhys Finch
fields.standfirst: Four thousand titles, no algorithm, and one rule about the second copy.
fields.image_alt: Ruled paper under a wide band of colour
fields.body:
People assume a small shop stocks the obvious things. It is closer to the opposite: the obvious things are everywhere already.

The second-copy rule

We only order a second copy of something one of us has read. It sounds precious. In practice it is the only way three people can keep one taste.

  • Everything face-out has been read by somebody here.
  • Everything on the table by the door arrived this week.
  • Nothing stays on the table for more than a month.

fields.author: Ada Marlow
fields.standfirst: Twenty-five chairs, one reader, and no obligation to say anything afterwards.
fields.image_alt: Four panes of a shop window seen from inside
fields.body:
The back room holds twenty-five people if nobody minds their knees. On the first Thursday of the month somebody reads for half an hour and then we all stand about for another one.

There is no sign-up and no charge. If you would like to read, say so at the counter; we are booked about two months ahead.

seo.description: Two rooms of new and second-hand books, a wall of prints, and somewhere to sit while you decide.

/about.title: The shop
/about.content: We are two rooms, three people and about four thousand books. We sell new and second-hand titles side by side, because that is how people actually read.

seo.description: Two rooms, three people and about four thousand books, on the same street since 1998.
Where to find us, and when. Tuesday to Saturday, ten until six, and Thursdays until nine.

/privacy.title: Privacy and accessibility
/privacy.content:
This is a placeholder. Replace it with your own privacy notice before you publish. Only you know what you do with the information this site collects, so only you can write it.

Say who you are and how to reach you; what the contact and newsletter forms collect, why, and how long you keep it; that the notice at the bottom of the page remembers its dismissal in the visitor's browser; anything you add that loads from another company, such as embedded videos, maps or scripts; and how someone can ask to see or delete what you hold about them.
